reason.description: Reason for block or approval requirement

approval_id.description:
Deterministic HITL queue entry UUID of the step's current hold,
present on a `require_approval` decision whose queue entry
exists. A step can be held more than once: hold 1 is UUID v5 over
`workflow_id + ":" + step_id`, and hold n >= 2 (a step held again
after its earlier hold was decided) is UUID v5 over
`workflow_id + ":" + step_id + "#" + n`. The approve and reject
responses carry the step's current hold's id (see their
`approval_id`). Returned by this route since #1082 but never
specced; added with `approval_enqueue` below,
which is only meaningful alongside it. Empty when no entry was
created (see `approval_enqueue`) AND on a cached replay
(`cached: true`, the default `retry_policy: "idempotent"` on a
step that was already evaluated), which reproduces the stored
decision without re-running the enqueue.

approval_enqueue.description:
What the HITL enqueue did for this gate. Present only on a
`require_approval` decision where an enqueue was attempted;
omitted otherwise.

A `require_approval` decision ALWAYS holds the step. This field is
how a client distinguishes "held, and there is a review entry to
approve" (`created` / `reused`) from "held, and there is nothing
to approve" (`cap_reached` / `tier_disabled` / `error`) - before
#3408's sibling fix those were the same response.

- `created` - a new queue entry was written. That includes a
  step held AGAIN after its earlier hold was decided (approved,
  rejected, expired or overridden): the re-hold is a new entry
  under the next hold's `approval_id`, with its own expiry and
  its own review, and the decided entry is kept unchanged as the
  record of that decision.
- `reused` - the gate resolved to the step's still-PENDING entry
  an earlier call created. The `approval_id` is the same. Reached
  only by a gate that is evaluated again while that entry is
  pending (`retry_policy: "reevaluate"`, a gate override, or
  concurrent gates of the step, where the gate admits them); the
  default `retry_policy: "idempotent"` replays the stored
  decision and carries `cached: true` with neither this field
  nor `approval_id`. A gate whose entry is already decided is
  never `reused`: it writes a new entry (`created`), or reports
  `error` when the queue refuses (for example, the hold id names
  an entry that belongs to another step, or the step has a queue
  entry outside its hold ids).
- `cap_reached` - the tenant is at its licence tier's
  `MaxPendingApprovals`. No entry was created and none will be
  until a pending one is resolved. **Not reachable by any shipped
  tier**: since HITL became Enterprise-only (2026-08-26) every
  entitled tier resolves `MaxPendingApprovals` to `-1`, and every
  tier with a finite cap is refused by the tier gate first.
  Documented because the mechanism is retained.
- `tier_disabled` - the deployment's licence tier does not enable
  HITL approvals. Entitled tiers are `Professional`, `Enterprise`
  and `Enterprise Plus`; `Community`, `Free`, `Pro`, `Premium` and
  `Evaluation` are refused. Approve, reject and the pending
  listings remain reachable on a refused tier so existing entries
  can still be drained.
- `error` - the enqueue failed for another reason; the detail is
  in `reason`.

policies_matched.description: Policies that matched and contributed to the decision (Issue

engine.description:
The engine that decided the step: `anchored`, the ADR-065 decision
plane (PRD v11 §1.1). Omitted on a cached replay (`cached: true`),
which reproduces a stored decision without deciding again.

subject_type.description:
The type of principal the step was decided for. Omitted on a
decision made before a subject was admitted, and wherever `engine`
is.

policy_bundle.description:
The digest of the policy set that decided the step. Omitted
wherever `subject_type` is.

cached.description:
**Deprecated (Issue #1673).** Whether this response was served from
a prior decision rather than a fresh policy evaluation. Use
`retry_context.gate_count > 1` instead — `cached` conflates
first-call-no vs many-retries-yes into a single bit. Kept
populated on every response for back-compat; removal planned
for a future major version.

decision_source.description:
**Deprecated (Issue #1673).** "fresh" or "cached". Use
`retry_context.prior_completion_status` for the distinction
agents and policies actually need. Kept populated on every
response for back-compat; removal planned for a future major.

PolicyMatch.description: Details of a policy match during evaluation (Issue

RetryContext.description:
First-class retry and execution state (Issue #1673 Phase 1). Always
present on every `StepGateResponse`, including the first gate call.
Replaces the ambiguous `cached: bool` signal with unambiguous state
the agent and policy engine can reason about.

gate_count.description:
Number of /gate calls for this (workflow_id, step_id), including
the current call. First call returns 1.

completion_count.description:
Number of /complete calls for this (workflow_id, step_id). Normally
0 on first gate, 1 after the step completes.

prior_completion_status.description:
"none" on first gate call. "completed" when a prior /gate + /complete
both landed. "gated_not_completed" when a prior /gate landed but no
/complete followed — uncertain territory the agent needs to reconcile
against the downstream system before re-executing.

prior_output_available.description:
True iff prior_completion_status == "completed". Mirrors whether
prior_output *could* be returned if include_prior_output=true.

prior_output.description:
Always present in the schema. Populated only when the caller set
?include_prior_output=true AND prior_output_available is true.
Otherwise null.

prior_completion_at.description: Timestamp of the prior /complete call, if any.

first_attempt_at.description:
Timestamp of the first /gate call for this step. On the first call,
equals last_attempt_at.

last_decision.description:
Decision of the immediately prior /gate call. On the first call
(gate_count == 1), equals the current decision (first-call
invariant).

idempotency_key.description:
The caller-supplied business-level key recorded on this step
(Issue #1673 Phase 2). Always present in the schema — empty
string `""` if the caller never supplied one.
